quiz_item.question: Why is a sharp carving knife safer than a dull blade when whittling or relief carving, and how should you protect your holding hand?
options: A. A dull blade slices through wood grain effortlessly, whereas a sharp blade requires you to push with your full body weight.
B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.
